newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may sell A Band cellular assets separately.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may sell A Band cellular assets separately.

text.p: Brazil's government is studying the possibility of splitting the cellular operations of publicly owned, state-level telecommunications companies and privatizing them separately, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.

The National Development Bank (BNDES) was due to report within 60 days on the advantages of selling the A Band services of subsidiaries of Telebras before the sale of the companies themselves, Motta said.

The minister said the government was concerned the upcoming privatization of B Band services, via 10 regional concessions, would expose the A Band services to fercious competition and undermine their value.
Should the BNDES decide it would be better to sell the A Band services separately, tender details for their privatization would be drawn up as soon as possible, Motta said.
The minister also said he expected the first two B Band contracts, for the Sao Paulo city and state areas, would be signed between May 15-20 with operations beginning in December.

The B Band program could be suspended, however, if Brazil's supreme court rules against the constitutionality of a so-called minimum law that lays down the framework for telecommunications privatization.
The Supreme Federal Tribunal was due to meet Wednesday afternoon although there were other items on its agenda.
